subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: The first Kalima i.e (Kalima-e-Tayyab) consists of how many dots ______?
didYouKnow: Kalima Tayyibah (لا إله إلا الله محمد رسول الله) is written using zero dotted Arabic letters (Nuqta)!
explanationEn: Topic: Beliefs (Aqaid) | Correct answer: A. 0

subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: Which Surah of the Quran has the name “Allah” in every single verse?
didYouKnow: Surah Al-Mujadila (Chapter 58) has 22 verses and repeats the Blessed Name "Allah" in every single verse.
explanationEn: Topic: The Holy Quran | Correct answer: B. Surah Al-Mujadila [58]

subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: How many Surah are with name of Prophets?
didYouKnow: Six Surahs carry a Prophet’s name: Yunus, Hud, Yusuf, Ibrahim, Muhammad, and Nuh (عليهم السلام).
explanationEn: Topic: The Holy Quran | Correct answer: C. 6

subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: ______ is known as “Saloos ul Quran”?
didYouKnow: Reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas once carries the reward equivalent to reading one-third (Saloos) of the Holy Quran!
explanationEn: Topic: The Holy Quran | Correct answer: A. Surah Ikhlas

subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: Which Sura is called ‘Aroos-ul-Qur’an (the Bride of the Qur’an)?
didYouKnow: Known as "Aroos-ul-Quran" (Bride of the Quran), Surah Ar-Rahman repeats its famous refrain 31 times.
explanationEn: Topic: The Holy Quran | Correct answer: D. Rahman

subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: Surah ______ is known as Heart of Quran.
didYouKnow: Surah Yaseen (Surah 36, 83 verses) is lovingly called "Qalb-ul-Quran" — the Heart of the Holy Quran.
explanationEn: Topic: The Holy Quran | Correct answer: D. Yaseen

subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: The Shortest Surah Al-Kawthar (الكوثر) has ______ verses?
didYouKnow: Surah Al-Kawthar is the shortest Surah with just 3 verses and 10 Arabic words — yet rich with eternal promise.
explanationEn: Topic: The Holy Quran | Correct answer: B. 3

subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: Surah Tauba the only Surah Which does not start with Bismillah is in Which Parah?
didYouKnow: Out of 114 Surahs, only Surah At-Tawbah begins without Bismillah — while Surah An-Naml mentions Bismillah twice, balancing to 114!
explanationEn: Topic: The Holy Quran | Correct answer: C. 10 & 11

subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: Who was the first person who counted the Aayath (verses) of the Qur’an?
didYouKnow: Umm-ul-Momineen Hazrat Ayesha (RA) was among the foremost scholars who preserved and counted the exact Quranic verses.
explanationEn: Topic: The Holy Quran | Correct answer: B. Hazart Ayesha(RA)

subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: ______ Surahs of the Holy Quran start with the word “Qul” (قل).
didYouKnow: Five Surahs begin with "Qul" (Say!): Al-Jinn, Al-Kafiroon, Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq, and An-Nas.
explanationEn: Topic: The Holy Quran | Correct answer: B. 5

subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: Ghaseel ul Malaika is the title of______?
didYouKnow: At Uhud, Hazrat Hanzala (RA) left his wedding night straight for jihad — and angels washed him, earning "Ghaseel-ul-Malaika".
explanationEn: Topic: Islamic History | Correct answer: C. Hazrat Hanzala (R.A)

subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: Who is known by the title 'Saifullah' (Sword of Allah)?
didYouKnow: Hazrat Khalid bin Walid (RA) fought in over 100 battles without ever suffering a single defeat!
explanationEn: Topic: Khulafa-e-Rashideen | Hazrat Khalid bin Walid (RA) was titled Saifullah.

subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: The first Msjid (Mosque) that was built by the Holy Prophet (SAW) was______?
didYouKnow: Masjid Quba was laid on the outskirts of Madinah immediately upon Hijrat — praying two rakats there equals the reward of an Umrah.
explanationEn: Topic: Seerat-un-Nabi (ﷺ) | Correct answer: B. Masjid e Quba

subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: Khateeb-ul-Ambia was the title of ______.
didYouKnow: Prophet Shoaib (AS) was honored with "Khateeb-ul-Anbiya" (Orator of the Prophets) for his unmatched eloquence.
explanationEn: Topic: Islamic History | Correct answer: D. Prophet Shoaib (A.S)

subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: Surah Ankaboot means ______?
didYouKnow: Surah Al-Ankaboot (29) uses the fragile spider’s web as a profound parable about relying on false powers.
explanationEn: Topic: The Holy Quran | Correct answer: D. Spider

subject: Islamic Studies
textEn: 27 attributes of Allah, mentioned in ______ Surah.
didYouKnow: Surah Al-Hadeed (Iron, Surah 57) opens with sweeping divine attributes — including Al-Awwal, Al-Akhir, Az-Zahir, Al-Batin.
explanationEn: Topic: The Holy Quran | Correct answer: D. Hadeed

subject: Biology
textEn: Heart beats about ______ times in one’s life.
didYouKnow: Your fist-sized heart pumps roughly 7,000+ liters daily — nearly 2.8 billion tireless beats over an average lifetime!
explanationEn: Topic: Transport System | Correct answer: A. 2.8 Billion

subject: Biology
textEn: The part of the brain that connects the two hemispheres of the brain is called______?
didYouKnow: The Corpus Callosum packs over 200 million nerve fibers linking the left and right halves of your brain in milliseconds.
explanationEn: Topic: Nervous & Chemical Coordination | Correct answer: A. Corpus callosum

subject: Biology
textEn: Which is the smallest gland in human body ______?
didYouKnow: Smaller than a grain of rice, the Pineal Gland secretes melatonin to keep your internal sleep-wake clock synced with darkness.
explanationEn: Topic: Nervous & Chemical Coordination | Correct answer: B. Pineal Gland

subject: Biology
textEn: Largest invertebrates is ______ ?
didYouKnow: Giant and Colossal Squids have eyes the size of dinner plates — the largest eyes in the entire animal kingdom!
explanationEn: Topic: Cell Biology | Correct answer: C. Squids

subject: Biology
textEn: Smallest disease causing agents in plants are ?
didYouKnow: Even simpler than viruses, Viroids have NO protein coat — just a tiny naked loop of infectious RNA!
explanationEn: Topic: Cell Biology | Correct answer: C. viroids

subject: Biology
textEn: Which is a parasitic plant?
didYouKnow: Cuscuta (Dodder / Amarbel) has zero chlorophyll — it latches onto host stems with microscopic suckers to steal sap!
explanationEn: Topic: Cell Biology | Correct answer: A. cuscuta

subject: Biology
textEn: In human body 99% of total mass is formed of______?
didYouKnow: Out of 90+ natural elements, just 6 (O, C, H, N, Ca, P) make up ~99% of your entire body weight!
explanationEn: Topic: Cell Biology | Correct answer: D. 6 Bio-elements

subject: Biology
textEn: Which bacterium is used in the production of insulin by genetic engineering?
didYouKnow: In 1978, scientists reprogrammed harmless E. coli bacteria to brew human insulin — ending lifelong dependence on animal pancreases.
explanationEn: Topic: Genetics & Biotechnology | Correct answer: C. Escherichia

subject: Biology
textEn: Deficiency of vitamin C will cause:______?
didYouKnow: Humans lost the active gene to make Vitamin C — unlike most animals, just a few weeks without citrus triggers Scurvy.
explanationEn: Topic: Nutrition & Digestion | Correct answer: C. Scurvy

subject: Biology
textEn: Tibia is a bone found in the ______?
didYouKnow: Your Tibia (shinbone) sits right beside the Fibula and is strong enough to bear multiples of your body weight on every stride.
explanationEn: Topic: Support & Movement | Correct answer: C. Leg

subject: Biology
textEn: ______ is essential for the formation of hemoglobin.
didYouKnow: Without just 4 Iron atoms inside every hemoglobin molecule, your red blood cells could not lock onto oxygen and turn bright red!
explanationEn: Topic: Biological Molecules | Correct answer: B. Iron

subject: Biology
textEn: Malaria is associated with______?
didYouKnow: Only the female Anopheles mosquito spreads malaria — she needs human blood protein solely to nourish her eggs.
explanationEn: Topic: Cell Biology | Correct answer: C. Anopheles Mosquito

subject: Biology
textEn: The expected number of RBCs in a single drop, or microliter, of blood is ______ million in Men.
didYouKnow: A single tiny microliter drop of human blood holds around 5 million oxygen-carrying red blood cells!
explanationEn: Topic: Transport System | Correct answer: A. 4.5 to 6.2 million

subject: Physics
textEn: The range of the projectile at 30 deg and 60 deg are__________________?
didYouKnow: Any two complementary launch angles (like 30° and 60°, or 15° and 75°) cover the exact same horizontal distance when ignoring air drag!
explanationEn: Topic: Kinematics | Correct answer: C. equal to each other

subject: Physics
textEn: What is the ratio of the velocity of sound at 4 atmosphere to that at 1 atmosphere?
didYouKnow: Double or quadruple air pressure at constant temperature and sound speed doesn’t budge at all (1 : 1) — only temperature & gas type change it!
explanationEn: Topic: Waves | Correct answer: B. 1 : 1

subject: Physics
textEn: The velocity of laser light is___________________?
optionsEn: Different for different colours or frequency
didYouKnow: A high-powered laser travels no faster than a pocket flashlight — both race through a vacuum at exactly c ≈ 3×10⁸ m/s!
explanationEn: Topic: Modern Physics | Correct answer: C. Equal to ordinary light

subject: Physics
textEn: Which of the following statements is true when we see ‘rainbow’ ?
optionsEn: The Sun remains behind us and we face raindrops
In light rainfall, we face Sun
The sky remains clear and the sun is at lower position in the sky
didYouKnow: You will NEVER spot a rainbow looking toward the Sun — sunlight must enter raindrops behind you, bounce internally at ~42°, and return!
explanationEn: Topic: Optics | Correct answer: B. The Sun remains behind us and we face raindrops

subject: Physics
textEn: Mirage is an example of ___________?
optionsEn: Refraction and total internal reflection of light
didYouKnow: A desert mirage isn’t a hallucination — superheated road air bends sky light upward via Total Internal Reflection, creating real watery puddles of sky!
explanationEn: Topic: Optics | Correct answer: C. Refraction and total internal reflection of light

subject: Physics
textEn: The speed of light will be minimum while passing through ?
didYouKnow: Light cruises at ~300,000 km/s in vacuum, slows by 25% in water, and drops to ~200,000 km/s inside dense crown glass!
explanationEn: Topic: Measurements | Correct answer: B. Glass

subject: Physics
textEn: One radian is equal to______________?
didYouKnow: One radian wraps an arc equal in length to the circle’s radius around the rim — which always measures ≈ 57.3°!
explanationEn: Topic: Circular Motion | Correct answer: B. 57.3°

subject: Physics
textEn: Tesla is the unit for measuring:
didYouKnow: Earth’s magnetic field is a gentle ~0.00005 Tesla — whereas a hospital MRI scanner generates a whopping 1.5 to 3 Tesla!
explanationEn: Topic: Electromagnetism | Correct answer: C. Magnetic induction

subject: Physics
textEn: Study of sound is called _____________?
didYouKnow: Faisal Mosque’s prayer hall and Greek amphitheaters use Acoustics — shaping sound reflections without needing microphones!
explanationEn: Topic: Waves | Correct answer: B. Acoustics

subject: Physics
textEn: The value of acceleration due to gravity is minimum on which of these planets?
didYouKnow: At only ~3.7 m/s², Mercury’s surface gravity is almost identical to Mars despite being far smaller — because of Mercury’s giant iron core!
explanationEn: Topic: Circular Motion | Correct answer: C. Mercury

subject: Physics
textEn: If a material object moves with speed of light its mass becomes ________________?
didYouKnow: Einstein’s relativity shows relativistic mass rockets toward infinity as v → c, which is why no object with rest mass can ever reach light speed!
explanationEn: Topic: Modern Physics | Correct answer: C. infinite

subject: Physics
textEn: Newton’s first law of motion gives the concept of _________?
didYouKnow: Your seatbelt saves you from Inertia — your body keeps moving forward at 100 km/h the instant your car brakes!
explanationEn: Topic: Dynamics | Correct answer: C. Inertia

subject: Chemistry
textEn: What is chemical symbol for Tungsten?
didYouKnow: Tungsten gets symbol "W" from its German mineral name "Wolframite" — and boasts the highest melting point of all metals (3,422 °C)!
explanationEn: Topic: General Chemistry | Correct answer: D. W

subject: Chemistry
textEn: The pH of milk is_______?
didYouKnow: Fresh milk is surprisingly slightly acidic (~pH 6.5–6.7) due to trace dissolved organic acids and casein proteins before souring even begins!
explanationEn: Topic: Equilibrium, Acids & Kinetics | Correct answer: B. 6.5-7

subject: Chemistry
textEn: Carbon,Diamond and Graphite are together called:___________?
didYouKnow: Pencil lead (soft graphite) and the hardest natural gem (diamond) are built from the EXACT same pure element: Carbon!
explanationEn: Topic: General Chemistry | Correct answer: A. Allotrope

subject: Chemistry
textEn: The molecules of CO2 in dry ice form__________________?
didYouKnow: "Dry ice" is solid CO₂ frozen below −78.5 °C — it skips the liquid phase completely and turns straight into misty fog!
explanationEn: Topic: General Chemistry | Correct answer: C. Molecular crystal

subject: Chemistry
textEn: Which of the following element has the maximum electron affinity_____?
didYouKnow: Even though Fluorine is most electronegative, Chlorine holds the highest Electron Affinity because its slightly larger orbitals handle an extra electron with less crowding!
explanationEn: Topic: Atomic Structure & Chemical Bonding | Correct answer: A. Cl

subject: Chemistry
textEn: The marsh gas is ___________?
didYouKnow: Bubbling out of swamps and wetlands as organic plants decay, Methane (CH₄) earned its classic nickname: "Marsh Gas".
explanationEn: Topic: Organic Chemistry | Correct answer: B. Methane

subject: Chemistry
textEn: Which one of the following is not the use of graphite ?
didYouKnow: Graphite feels silky slippery because flat hexagonal carbon sheets slide past each other like a deck of cards — the exact opposite of an abrasive!
explanationEn: Topic: Electrochemistry | Correct answer: B. Abrasive

subject: Chemistry
textEn: Which one is Chloroform_________________?
didYouKnow: Chloroform (CHCl₃) was first used in medicine in 1847 and differs from greenhouse solvent CCl₄ by a single Hydrogen atom!
explanationEn: Topic: General Chemistry | Correct answer: C. CHCl3

subject: Chemistry
textEn: The law which states that the amount of gas dissolved in a liquid is proportional to its partial pressure is___________?
didYouKnow: Henry’s Law explains why a sealed soda bottle stays fizzy — pop the cap, pressure drops, and dissolved CO₂ rushes out as bubbles!
explanationEn: Topic: Stoichiometry & Solutions | Correct answer: C. Henry’s law

subject: Chemistry
textEn: The molecular formula of Methane gas is___________?
didYouKnow: Natural Sui gas used for cooking across Pakistan is roughly 90%+ pure Methane (CH₄) — the simplest hydrocarbon molecule!
explanationEn: Topic: Organic Chemistry | Correct answer: B. CH4

subject: Pakistan Studies
textEn: Buttons Made From Seashell Were Used In The Indus Valley Civilization By ______ BCE.
didYouKnow: Wait — humans were using sculpted seashell buttons as ornamental fasteners in the Indus Valley around 2500 BCE — 4,500 years ago!
explanationEn: Correct answer: D. 2500

subject: Pakistan Studies
textEn: All Indus Valley Bricks Were The Same Ratio Of ______.
didYouKnow: From Mohenjo-Daro to Harappa across 1.25 million sq km, ancient builders fired kiln bricks in the exact universal 1 : 2 : 4 engineering ratio!
explanationEn: Correct answer: B. 1:2:4

subject: Pakistan Studies
textEn: The Smallest Cube Used As Weight Weighed Less Than ______ Gram.
didYouKnow: Indus Valley jewelers used polished stone cube weights down to < 1 gram — the precision gold-weight ancestors of modern scales!
explanationEn: Correct answer: A. 1

subject: Pakistan Studies
textEn: The Senate Has ______ Members.
didYouKnow: Unlike the National Assembly, Pakistan’s Senate is a permanent house (104 seats historically enshrined in the Constitution) where half retire every 3 years.
explanationEn: Correct answer: A. 104

subject: Pakistan Studies
textEn: Article 19 Of The Constitution Guarantees The Right To ______.
didYouKnow: Article 19 (and Article 19-A Right to Information) protects freedom of expression and press freedom in Pakistan’s 1973 Constitution!
explanationEn: Correct answer: C. Freedom Of Speech

subject: World Capitals - Oceania
textEn: What is the capital of Australia?
didYouKnow: Sydney and Melbourne argued so fiercely over which should be capital that Australia built a brand-new planned city right between them: Canberra!
explanationEn: Correct answer: B. Canberra

subject: World Capitals - Americas
textEn: What is the capital of Bolivia?
didYouKnow: Sucre is Bolivia’s official constitutional capital — though executive ministries sit high in La Paz, making it one of the world’s few dual-capital countries!
explanationEn: Correct answer: D. Sucre

subject: World Capitals - Americas
textEn: What is the capital of Brazil?
didYouKnow: Rio de Janeiro lost capital status in 1960 when Brazil built modernist Brasília in the interior savannah in just 41 months!
explanationEn: Correct answer: A. Brasília

subject: World Capitals - Americas
textEn: What is the capital of Canada?
didYouKnow: Not Toronto, Montreal, or Vancouver — Queen Victoria chose small lumber-town Ottawa in 1857 to sit peacefully along the English–French border!
explanationEn: Correct answer: B. Ottawa

subject: World Capitals - Europe
textEn: What is the capital of Switzerland?
didYouKnow: Switzerland technically avoids calling any city a formal capital, designating Bern simply as its historical "Federal City"!
explanationEn: Correct answer: C. Bern

subject: World Capitals - Asia
textEn: What is the capital of Turkey?
didYouKnow: Istanbul is Turkey’s largest and most famous city across two continents, yet Ankara has served as the modern capital since 1923!
explanationEn: Correct answer: B. Ankara

subject: World Currencies - Asia
textEn: What is the official currency of Kuwait?
didYouKnow: The Kuwaiti Dinar (KWD) consistently ranks as the highest-valued currency unit per 1 note on planet Earth!
explanationEn: Correct answer: C. Kuwaiti dinar

subject: Aptitude
textEn: A clock is started at noon. By 10 minutes past 5, the hour hand has turned through:
didYouKnow: An hour hand sweeps 30° per hour AND 0.5° every single minute — in 5h 10m (310 minutes), 310 × 0.5° = 155°!
explanationEn: Angle traced by hour hand in 12 hrs = $${360^ \circ }$$ Angle traced by hour hand in 5 hrs 10 min. i.e., $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{31}}{6}{\text{hrs}} = {\left( {\frac{{360}}{{12}} \times \frac{{31}}{6}} \right)^ \circ } \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = {155^ \circ } \end{aligned}$$

subject: Aptitude
textEn: The angle between the minute hand and the hour hand of a clock when the time is 4:20, is:
didYouKnow: Surprise! At 4:20 the hands aren’t overlapping — the hour hand quietly drifted 10° past the 4 mark!
explanationEn: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Angle}}\,{\text{traced}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{hour}}\,{\text{hand}}\,{\text{in}}\,\frac{{13}}{3}\,{\text{hrs}} \\ & = {\left( {\frac{{360}}{{12}} \times \frac{{13}}{3}} \right)^ \circ } = {130^ \circ } \\ & {\text{Angle}}\,{\text{tra ced}}\,{\text{by}}\,{\text{min}}{\text{.}}\,{\text{hand}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{20}}\,{\text{min}} \\ & = {\left( {\frac{{360}}{{60}} \times 20} \right)^ \circ } = {120^ \circ } \\ & \therefore {\text{Required}}\,{\text{angle}} \\ & = {\left( {130 - 120} \right)^ \circ } \\ & = {10^ \circ } \end{aligned}$$

subject: Aptitude
textEn: How many times are the hands of a clock at right angle in a day?
didYouKnow: In 24 hours, clock hands form 90° not 48 times, but 44 times — skipping 4 collisions around 3:00 and 9:00!
explanationEn: In 12 hours, they are at right angles 22 times. ∴ In 24 hours, they are at right angles 44 times.

subject: Aptitude
textEn: How many times do the hands of a clock coincide in a day?
didYouKnow: Over 12 hours hands overlap only 11 times (the 11–12–1 zone shares a single overlap at 12:00), making 22 times in 24 hours!
explanationEn: The hands of a clock coincide 11 times in every 12 hours (Since between 11 and 1, they coincide only once, i.e., at 12 o'clock). AM 12:00 1:05 2:11 3:16 4:22 5:27 6:33 7:38 8:44 9:49 10:55 PM 12:00 1:05 2:11 3:16 4:22 5:27 6:33 7:38 8:44 9:49 10:55 The hands overlap about every 65 minutes, not every 60 minutes. ∴ The hands coincide 22 times in a day.

subject: Aptitude
textEn: It was Sunday on Jan 1, 2006. What was the day of the week Jan 1, 2010?
didYouKnow: Each ordinary year shifts Jan 1 forward by 1 weekday, and 2008 was a Leap Year (+2)! So 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = +5 days → Friday!
explanationEn: On 31 st December, 2005 it was Saturday. Number of odd days from the year 2006 to the year 2009 = (1 + 1 + 2 + 1) = 5 days. ∴ On 31 st December 2009, it was Thursday. Thus, on 1 st Jan, 2010 it is Friday.

subject: Aptitude
textEn: What was the day of the week on 28 th May, 2006?
didYouKnow: Using odd-day modular arithmetic, 28 May 2006 hits 0 odd days mod 7 — landing cleanly on Sunday!
explanationEn: 28 May, 2006 = (2005 years + Period from 1.1.2006 to 28.5.2006) Odd days in 1600 years = 0 Odd days in 400 years = 0 5 years = (4 ordinary years + 1 leap year) = (4 x 1 + 1 x 2) ≡ 6 odd days Jan. Feb. March April May (31 + 28 + 31 + 30 + 28 ) = 148 days ∴ 148 days = (21 weeks + 1 day) ≡ 1 odd day. Total number of odd days = (0 + 0 + 6 + 1) = 7 ≡ 0 odd day. Given day is Sunday.

subject: English Grammar Section 2
textEn: I . . . . . always capital.
didYouKnow: Grammar trick! Here "I" refers to the word/letter "I" itself (singular noun), NOT the speaker — so singular "is" takes it!
explanationEn: Correct answer: B. is

subject: English Grammar Section 1
textEn: The scientific study of the human mind and behaviour is called . . . . . .
didYouKnow: Psychology stems from Greek "psyche" (soul/mind/breath) + "-logia" — literally "study of the mind".
explanationEn: Correct answer: D. Psychology

subject: Computer Science
textEn: What is the default port for HTTP traffic?
didYouKnow: Plain unencrypted HTTP uses Port 80, while padlock-encrypted HTTPS listens next door on Port 443!
explanationEn: Port 80 is the standard port for HTTP.

subject: Computer Science
textEn: Which data structure operates on a Last In First Out (LIFO) basis?
didYouKnow: Like a stack of plates in a cafeteria — your web browser’s Back button and Undo history work as a LIFO Stack!
explanationEn: A Stack follows LIFO order.
